analysis.title: Global Multi-Industry: Key Takeaways from SEMICON Europa
key_insights: Semiconductor equipment demand is very strong with no signs of customer hesitation or slowing order momentum, based on GS meetings at SEMICON Europa (Munich, 11 Nov) with VAT, Ebara, Pfeiffer Vacuum, Inficon and Edwards Vacuum.

The shift to advanced-node production means more vacuum chambers are needed for the additional process steps. VAT says customer planning windows now extend 3 quarters ahead (vs 2 historically, some planning September 2027 deliveries) and lead times are 3-4 months.

Ebara's backlog is about 12 months, twice the normal ~6 months, and it expects to deliver 5,500 vacuum pumps next year. Pfeiffer Vacuum and Edwards say their lead times have not materially lengthened because of capacity expansions over the past 2 years.

The capacity ramp is straining the supply chain. Ebara cites raw metal parts as a bottleneck and Pfeiffer cites frequency inverters (1-2 per dry pump, with embedded microcontrollers). Edwards has diversified every product to at least two sites, including dry pumps in Korea and Genesee, New York.

Pricing power is strong for dominant players. VAT has put through about 10% pricing this year with >70% share in leading-edge processes. Pfeiffer can raise prices 1-2 times a year in Europe but faces more intense competition in Asia.

Sub-fab equipment makers face more competition than cleanroom equipment makers. Ebara says there are many Chinese dry vacuum pump competitors, driven by China's localization push to >50% self-sufficiency in chip tools.

Services are a focus to smooth WFE cycle volatility. VAT expects field services growth to accelerate next year as retrofits/upgrades (30% of services) are currently deferred by customers, with a further uptick beyond 2027/28E as the installed base leaves warranty.

Edwards' new Ganymede dry pump uses 60% less energy than the prior generation. Ebara says its machines are 14% more energy efficient than competitors. Inficon's FabGuard software monitors chamber gas in real time.

Chinese competitors have not yet been seen outside their local markets. VAT is less concerned about further US export restrictions because of its dominant share among local equipment OEMs, and Inficon and Edwards have plants in China supplying local foundries.

VAT: order inflow is at a similar level to 2Q26, with a possible good quarter if it accelerates into year-end (CHF 20-30mn pre-buy). China growth expectations are now low double digit vs mid-to-high single digit at the start of the year, and the region is margin accretive.

VAT is likely to give quantitative 2027E revenue guidance with FY26 results in March, and says revenue 15-20% above the top of the previous range (CHF1.5-1.7bn from the 2025 CMD) is feasible and even conservative.

VAT capacity: factory output run-rate is CHF450mn, ~1,000 hires YTD, and the Malaysia 1B factory opens 1Q27, taking total capacity to CHF2.5bn. Management flags normal 1Q27 seasonality from Chinese New Year effects on Malaysia sales.
VAT guided FY2026 EBITDA margin of 32-33% (Visible Alpha consensus 33.5%), with 2H above 35% (consensus 36.1%). Margins should continue to rise in 2027E on operating leverage despite ramp costs.

VAT sees ALD valves and other adjacencies reaching 20% of group sales by 2029. It sees Presys (acquired by Atlas Copco) as a competitor in isolation valves (10-20% of VAT sales), while its strength is in control valves.

Ebara holds a top-2 position in dry vacuum pumps with a 250k installed base. About 150 additional process steps arise in the move to 2nm, each needing an additional pump. Ebara's EV-M uses 18 SLM nitrogen vs ~22 SLM for Edwards.
GS targets: VAT Group CHF 874 (12-month, sector-relative EV/IC to ROIC/WACC), Ebara ¥7,900 (implying FY12/27E P/E 25x and P/B 5.6x).

market_movers.rationale: VAT sees no slowdown in demand, rising backlog visibility and possible 2027 revenue 15-20% above the top of prior guidance. Not US-listed.
Ebara backlog is about twice normal and it expects to deliver 5,500 vacuum pumps next year. Raw metal parts are the main supply constraint. Not US-listed.

sector_views.rationale: Order momentum is strong, planning windows are lengthening and pricing power is strong for dominant players. Services and advanced-node process complexity support growth.

earnings_insights: VAT guided FY2026 EBITDA margin of 32-33% vs Visible Alpha consensus 33.5%, and 2H26 above 35% vs consensus 36.1%.
VAT order inflow is at a similar level to 2Q26, and 4Q could be a good quarter with CHF 20-30mn of pre-buy if it accelerates with normal seasonality.
VAT is expected to give 2027E revenue guidance with FY26 results in March. It says 15-20% above the top end of the 2025 CMD range (CHF1.5-1.7bn) is feasible.
VAT FY2025 EBITDA margin in services was 45.6% (the report says >50% historical margins are possible again beyond 2027/28E).
risk_factors: VAT: delays in sales conversion from capacity ramp constraints.
VAT: further US export restrictions on WFE equipment to China.
VAT: emerging competition from China-based valve producers.
VAT: FX headwinds or ramp-up cost headwinds.
VAT: delays in memory/logic capex leading to order cancellations, or concerns about AI capex sustainability.
Ebara: a semiconductor capex downcycle, tougher Chinese CMP competition, slow adoption of new device technology, lower crude/LNG prices and weaker refining/petrochemical margins.
geopolitical: Further US export restrictions on WFE equipment to China are a flagged risk, though VAT is less concerned given its dominant share among local equipment OEMs.
China's localization push targets >50% self-sufficiency in semiconductor manufacturing tools, which drives adoption of local equipment.
